title: Locale-aware promptset coverage map (CJK + RTL)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a coverage map and quick design for a reusable multilocale promptset focused on: CJK (zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ja, ko) and RTL (ar, fa, he).
It combines locale-formatting checks, translation/roundtrip smoke tests, and bidi/display edgecases. The goal is a compact, high-signal set we can run in onboarding and regression suites without blowing up runtime.

Goals and constraints:
- Surface regressions that affect user-visible formatting (dates, numbers, punctuation, whitespace, quotes, currency).
- Catch common bidi rendering & logical-flows for RTL languages (mirrored punctuation, numerals in LTR spans, mixed-script ordering).
- Quick translation quality indicators: adequacy (content preserved), hallucination flags, named-entity fidelity.
- Keep promptset to ~150-300 prompts per language group (not per locale) to be runnable in nightly/eval runs.
- Provide clear heuristics for pass/fail that avoid false positives for stylistic variance.

Scope and selection heuristics:
- Prioritize short to medium prompts (8–80 tokens), because most regressions appear on shorter sequences.
- For formatting checks, include both isolated tokens (e.g., date string) and contextualized sentences ("Please schedule for 2026/03/05 at 14:30") to capture parsing/normalization.
- Translation checks include: source->target direct translation plus target->source roundtrip where applicable. Automatic metrics (BLEU/ChrF) used only as signals; human spot-checks for high-delta failures.
- Include a small subset of long prompts (>= 150 tokens) to catch KV-cache/attention issues.

Categories and representative cases (coverage map):
1) Dates & Times
   - Formats: yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy/MM/dd, dd.MM.yyyy, localized full dates (e.g., '2026年3月5日', '5 مارس 2026').
   - Edgecases: month names in mixed script, weekday abbreviations, ordinal indicators (English), Japanese era names (brief).
   - Example prompt: "Convert '2026/03/05 14:30' to the local long date for zh-Hant and ar."

2) Numbers & Grouping
   - Thousands separator differences (comma vs. space vs. none), decimal marks (dot vs. comma), full-width digits (CJK), Indic digits (Arabic-Indic).
   - Example prompt: "Format 1234567.89 for ko and ar in currency style."

3) Currency & Units
   - Symbol placement, non-breaking spaces, pluralization rules.
   - Example prompt: "Display 'USD 2,500' as local currency for ja and fa."

4) Quotation marks & punctuation
   - Nested quotes (Chinese corner quotes 「」, Japanese 『』, English “ ”), mirrored punctuation in RTL, IDEOGRAPHIC vs ASCII punctuation.
   - Example prompt: "Rewrite: He said, \"I’ll be there at 5:00 pm.\" for zh-Hans and ar preserving quote style."

5) BiDi & Mixed-script ordering
   - Sentences mixing English and Arabic/Hebrew, numerals inside RTL runs, punctuation anchoring.
   - Failure signals: reordering of LTR named entities, orphaned punctuation on wrong side.
   - Example prompt: "Translate and preserve the order: 'Call Alice at 03/05/2026, رقم: 555-0123' into ar and then back to en."

6) Named-entity fidelity
   - Person/place names, product names, acronyms: prefer transliteration vs. translation policies per locale.
   - Example prompt: "Translate 'Redwood Inference launched v1.2' to ja; should keep 'Redwood Inference' as proper noun."

7) Locale-specific abbreviations & calendars
   - Japanese era notation, Persian calendar mentions (where applicable), weekday-first conventions.
   - Example prompt: "Convert Monday, March 15 2026 into ja era-style and fa-friendly display."

8) Translation adequacy & hallucination checks
   - Short prompts that are semantically precise to detect missing or injected content.
   - Example prompt: "Summarize: 'The mayor canceled the parade due to heavy rain.'" (expect conservative paraphrase).

9) Tokenization/segmentation artifacts
   - CJK segmentation edgecases with numbers and Latin acronyms, spacing insertion/removal.
   - Example prompt: "Tokenize and then detokenize the headline: 'AI突破: Chat-LLM v2.0发布' for zh-Hant and ja."

Promptset composition (proposed counts):
- Core formatting primitives (shared across locales): 40 prompts
- CJK-specific templates: 70 prompts (split zh-Hans/zh-Hant/ja/ko variations)
- RTL-specific templates: 70 prompts (ar/fa/he with script-appropriate numerals)
- Translation & roundtrip smoke: 80 prompts (paired source sentences + expected fidelity checks)
- Long-form stress samples: 20 prompts
Total: ~280 prompts (we'll parameterize to produce per-locale permutations; the above totals are group-level).

Evaluation metrics and pass/fail heuristics:
- Formatting checks: exact match on normalized canonical form (we define canonical normalization for each test). Allow normalized whitespace differences; fail if punctuation type or order differs.
- BiDi checks: structural assertions (named-entity order preserved, punctuation attached to correct run). Use simple regex heuristics + visual spot-checks.
- Translation adequacy: if automatic metric (ChrF) drops >0.12 or BLEU delta >8 between baseline and candidate, flag for triage.
- Hallucination: presence of named entities or facts not in source -> immediate flag. Use entity-list comparison.
- Regression severity levels: minor (stylistic), medium (formatting visible to user), major (incorrect facts, wrong order that changes meaning).

Automation & tooling notes:
- Prompts are generated from parameterized templates (seeded examples + locale-specific tokens). Keep template repo small and human-reviewable.
- For bidi rendering checks, we will output codepoints and logical-order checks rather than relying on visual rendering in CI. We keep a small set of screenshots for manual verification of high-severity failures.
- Roundtrip flow: source -> target -> back-to-source -> compare with fuzzy thresholds. For languages with multiple canonical forms (zh-Hans/zH-Hant), compare normalized forms using Unicode NFKC + locale mapping table.

Human review plan:
- Any flagged test for translation adequacy (high delta) gets sent to a small pool of reviewers (L2) for spot-check within 48 hours.
- Monthly calibration: sample 10% of passing tests for human review to detect false negatives.

Quick sample prompts (clipboard-ready) – do not duplicate in other corpora:
- CJK date contextual: "用户: 请把 '2026/03/05 14:30' 转换为中文(繁體)完整日期格式。"
- RTL mixed-order: "Customer: Please call محمد at 14:00 on 5/3/2026 — number ٠٥٥٥٠١٢٣. Translate to English preserving number order."
- Quotation style: "Rewrite: She said, 'I'll go.' for ja using native Japanese quotes."
- Currency placement: "Format '2500 USD' for ko as a localized currency string."

Open questions & risks:
- Should we store expected canonical forms for all permutations (heavy maintenance) vs. derive expectations via small deterministic normalization library? Recommendation: derive expectations via normalization + a small per-locale override table.
- Persian calendars: are we required to convert Gregorian dates to Solar Hijri in some customer use-cases? Need product input.
- How to handle locale fallback: when model returns variant wording (e.g., different but correct translation), automatic metric may flag it. Human review backlog risk.

Action items:
- [Sana] Build parameterized template repo and generate first pass (~280 prompts) — due 2026-01-10.
- [Jun] Implement normalization library and canonical mapping table — due 2026-01-17.
- [Laila] Setup Chromedriver screenshot harness for 10 canonical bidi cases — due 2026-01-24.
- [Marcus] Add roundtrip evaluation glue with ChrF baseline scoring and alerts — due 2026-01-20.

References and notes:
- See Confluence locale eval index (linked above) for prior smaller promptbanks.
- Avoid duplicating the 'quickcheck' corpus; this doc is explicitly a synthesis/coverage map to guide generation.

Status: draft — soliciting feedback on counts, pass thresholds, and whether to include additional languages (hi, th) in baseline run or in a secondary expansion.

Notes to reviewers: focus feedback on the heuristics for bidi and translation adequacy thresholds. If you have sample edgecases we missed, paste them inline and tag the action owner.
